← Macro dashboard

Options positioning

From Cboe's free delayed option chains, taken at each update (after the US close, and hourly in US hours on weekdays once hourly updates are on): open interest is the settled figure from the start of the session; prices are the latest available at the time shown on the desk, not necessarily closes. Gamma exposure assumes dealers hold the opposite side of customers who are long calls and long puts, a common simplification; it maps where hedging flows may cluster, not where price must go. S&P levels come from SPX options and are shifted to ES by the current ES minus SPX gap; gold levels come from GLD options scaled to the COMEX gold future. Not a live trade tape.

How to read this

Likely range this week is the 68% range (±1 sigma) from the last 20 and 60 days of price swings. In a 2001-2026 test on 7 pairs the weekly move stayed inside it 68.3% of weeks, so it is a size estimate you can rely on.

Macro lean counts the drivers that support the instrument higher or lower (a net of 2 is a lean). In the same test the read was right only about half of weeks, so treat it as background, not a signal. Crowded positioning (Z of 2 or more) and the risk or volatility rows are shown but not counted.

Confluence score (0-100) combines momentum, RSI, trend and Z-score; 60 or more reads bullish, 40 or less bearish. It also showed no reliable edge in the backtest.

Pairs use ECB reference rates, gold uses COMEX futures, indices are the S&P 500, Nasdaq 100 and Dow 30 cash levels (Yahoo Finance, FRED as fallback). Latest data 2026-11-19 (pairs: ECB fixing; gold and indices: last price of the latest update). The chart shows % change from the start of the selected range.
